2.  The respondent No. 1 as plaintiff instituted the aforesaid suit for partition of the suit-lands and for allotment of Saham in respect of his share on declaration of his title thereto. Plaintiffs case, briefly, was that the 1st schedule land of the plaint which includes the 2nd schedule-land belonged to the present defendant No. 1 Abdur Rahman and defendant No. 2 Md. Ilias jointly in equal shares which were recorded in the RS Khatian accordingly; that defendant No. 3 Jobeda Khatoon who is the divorced wife of defendant No. 1 Abdur Rahman obtained a decree in M S No. 31/46 of the Court of Munsif, Cox's Bazar for dower-debt and then purchased defendant, Abdur Rahman's share in the Money Execution Case No. 34/48 on 7-4-48; that in pursuance thereof obtained delivery of possession in the suit-land i.e. in Abdur Rahman's share after auction purchase. Subsequently she settled six kanis of land out of her auction purchased land with defendants No. 4-9 on 28-7-55 on the basis of a patta vide Ext. 1; that the defendants No. 4-9 possessed the said six kanis of land and thereafter defendant Nos. 4-6 and 8 sold their four kanis of land out of the said holding to the plaintiff on the basis of a registered kabala dated 24-12-58 vide Ext. 2; that plaintiffs vendor later on executed an antedated kabala in favour of the defendant No. 10 in respect of their share in the suit-land in collusion with defendant No. 1 Abdur Raham to defeat plaintiffs title; that the plaintiff possessed the suit-land but the same was wrongly recorded in the name of defendant No. 1 Abdur Rahman Hence the suit by the plaintiff for declaration of title and for partition and allotment of saham in respect of the said schedule of land of the plaint. 

 19. Mr. Niaz Muhammad, the learned Advocate for the defendant appellant however cited 2 decisions one in the case of MP Krishnawami Pillai vs. Chockalingam Chettiar and others reported in AIR 1943 Madras 455 and another in the case of Sarjaraz Ali Khan vs. Abdul Ghafur Khan and others, reported in AIR 1929 Lahore 81 to show that as because there is no discussion by the court below on a certain point in the judgment it cannot be concluded that the point was not raised or argued in the court below, I however, respectfully agree with the view as taken in the above decisions and differed with the contention of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff respondent and, as such, it cannot be held conclusively that the point on estoppel was not raised by the defendant-appellant in the court of appeal below because of the absence of any discussion or finding on the same in the impugned judgment. Now, it is the contention of the learned Advocate for the appellant that as regards other points involved in the case namely, whether the defendant-appellant had knowledge of the Money Suit of defendant No. 3 i.e. MS No. 31/46 and the M Execution case No. 34 of 1984 and in pursuance thereof the auction purchase by defendant No. 3 vide Ext. 6 and then the transfer of the land by her by a Patta to defendant Nos. 4-9 vide Ext. 9, thereafter the purchase by the plaintiff vide Ext. 2, he does not like to make any submission as the same has been concluded by finding of facts by both the courts below. But his main grievance is with regard to the question of estoppel. His submission is that admittedly the plaintiff-respondent along with others instituted a money suit for contribution being Money Suit No.45/57 against the contesting defendant Abdur Rahman as well as some other co-sharers and the same was decreed and in pursuance thereof Money Execution No.63/61 was started and in that Money Execution Case, the contesting defendant Abdur Rahman paid his share of the contribution money in court which was withdrawn by the plaintiff and as such he admitted the contesting defendant's title and interest in the suit-holding and hence the subsequent suit brought against him i.e. the contesting defendant, and others by the plaintiff is barred by estoppel in view of section 115 of the Evidence Act, but unfortunately this point has been wrongly decided against the defendant by the trial Court with a finding that the suit was not barred by estoppel and the lower appellate Court failed to consider this vital point of estoppel at all but somehow affirmed the decision of the trial Court only with some modification with regard to the quantum of land of the schedule and hence the impugned judgment is not a proper and valid judgment which is liable to be set aside. 

 25. The contention of the learned Advocate for the respondent is that the plaintiff even before his purchase was a co-sharer along with the other defendants and the money suit for contribution was not instituted by plaintiff alone, it was instituted by the plaintiff along with some other co-sharers against the contesting co-sharer defendant and some other defendant-co-sharers, and so far the status of the contesting defendant is concerned, it is not disputed that he is a co-sharer in the suit-holding but his interest to the extent of 4 kanis of land which the defendant No. 3 first auction-purchased in execution of a money decree and then transferred it to defendant Nos. 4-9 by a patta who again sold out the same to the plaintiff-respondent by registered deed and thereby the right, title and interest of the contesting defendant was already extinguished and the same ultimately devolved upon the plaintiff-respondent and this was well within the knowledge of the contesting defendant and thus the subsequent suit for contribution by the plaintiff and others as against the defendants, particularly the defendant No. 1, cannot be constituted as any actual admission of his right, title; interest in the said 4 kanis of land of the plaintiff. The contesting defendant might have some interest of some share in the suit-holding as his co-shareship in the same was not disputed by the plaintiff. The plaintiff- respondent is however concerned only with his own share of 4 kanis of land in the schedule property which he purchased from defendant Nos. 4-6 and 8. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondent. further contends that' the institution of the suit for contribution and its execution thereof has not changed or altered the condition or position of the contesting defendant even in respect of his possession in some portion over the same. The learned Advocate in support of his contention has cited two decisions, one in the case of Kista Chandra Mandal and others vs. Mt.
